name: Devil’s Father

attributes.attribute: haunted wakes hoping to meet his son
had three legs and a red tail
unlike the Devil's Mother in origin

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Devil's Father is an Irish folkloric figure. His other names are Duveruckan and Duvephucan. He is unlike the Devil's Mother. The Devil's Mother draws on ancient goddesses. She also draws on pagan mythological monsters. The Devil's Father seems entirely invented. He appeared after the Christianization of Ireland. He haunted wakes. He hoped to meet his son there. His son was expected to steal the soul of the dead. The Devil's Father was easy to recognize. He had three legs. He had a red tail. He carried a phallus-shaped walking stick. These marks made him unmistakable at a wake. He came only to take the soul of the dead. His purpose was fixed. His form gave him away at once. The figure served a folk purpose after conversion.

okr.objective: Describe the Irish folkloric Devil's Father and his marks of recognition.
key_results: Give the names Duveruckan and Duvephucan
Contrast his invented origin with the Devil's Mother's ancient roots
